boundary: a stock Meshtastic node's own log, receiving a PKI direct message built entirely by tethermesh
what_this_proves: L6's second direction: emitting a direct message an unmodified reference node accepts. The first direction (decrypting one they sent) is covered by pki_dm_record.json.

provenance.receiver: Heltec V3, stock Meshtastic 2.7.26.54e0d8d, unmodified, region US, LongFast

our_frame.hex: 64e769330100577e210dad0b6300000147...  (48 bytes; id and extra_nonce vary per run)

confirmations.what: nonce construction, confirmed from the far side
confirmations.detail: The receiver logged the nonce it used: 21 0d ad 0b | 21 0d 00 52 | 01 00 57 7e | 00. That is packet_id LE (0x0bad0d21), extra_nonce LE (0x52000d21), from LE (0x7e570001), then 0x00 - exactly the construction WIRE_REFERENCE.md records, now observed being reconstructed independently by the reference implementation.

The receiver logged its derived key prefix as d8 85 d2 24 e6 cc 3d e0, identical to the value already recorded in WIRE_REFERENCE.md from the inbound direction. Our X25519 and SHA-256 KDF produce the same key a stock node does, now demonstrated in BOTH directions.
PKI Decryption worked! / Packet decrypted using PKI! / Received text msg from=0x7e570001, id=0xbad0d21, msg=tethermesh-pki-1 - decoded at Portnum=1 and marked PKI.

incidental_observation.detail: On relaying our broadcast NodeInfo the node logged: 'rx_snr found. hop_limit:2 rx_snr:6.750000' then 'rx_snr found in packet. Setting tx delay:3360'. At 6.75 dB SNR it chose a 3360 ms transmit delay, which at the 28 ms slot time is 120 slots.
incidental_observation.why_this_is_not_a_resolution: One sample cannot separate a deterministic delay from a single draw out of a random window, and gives no second point to fit a slope. It bounds nothing on its own. Recorded because it is the first direct observation of the mechanism WIRE_REFERENCE.md item 7 lists as unverified, and because a sweep across SNR would settle that item.
